claim_1.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of peripheral blood cells / whole blood RNA samples from 92 individuals measured before vaccination (day 0) and on days 1, 3, and 14 after vaccination showed that maximum gene-expression changes occurred in the initial 24 hours after vaccination, with 4740 transcripts changing after vaccination and the maximum expression change occurring on day 1.

sources.quote: We identified expression changes in 4740 transcripts (Dataset 1) after imposing a FDR cutoff of 0.01 on the P value for the day effect.
The maximum expression change occurred on day 1, while day 14 had the greatest number of genes with maximum expression values.

claim_2.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of peripheral blood cells / whole blood RNA samples after trivalent influenza vaccination showed three distinct temporal expression patterns—early upregulation, late upregulation, and downregulation—with early upregulated genes enriched for interferon response, antigen processing and presentation, and JAK/STAT and NFκB-related pathways, whereas late responses suggested increased protein biosynthesis and cellular proliferation.

sources.quote: A visual summary of the dynamic changes in the transcriptional response to vaccination over time shows three major gene expression patterns: downregulation, early upregulation, and late upregulation (Figure 1A).
Associations were most significant for the interferon response pathway (GO:0005062, GO:0034341, and GO:0034340) when compared with other cytokines.
Activation of antigen processing and presentation is implied by the increased expression of major histocompatibility complex (MHC) Class I genes (eg, GO:002474).

Of the signal transduction pathways, the Janus kinase/signal transducers and activators of transcription (JAK/STAT) (GO:007259) and nuclear factor kappa beta (NFκβ) (GO:0043122) axes were particularly enriched.

In contrast, the late vaccine response was characterized by increased detection of transcripts for genes involved in intracellular processes suggestive of active cellular proliferation, including macromolecule biosynthesis (eg, GO:0009059), cellular protein metabolism (eg, GO:0044267), RNA metabolic processing (eg, GO:0016070), and regulation of antiapoptosis (GO:0045767).

groups.tissue_type: peripheral blood cells / whole blood RNA samples

claim_3.claim: Hemagglutination Inhibition and Neutralizing Antibody Titer Assay analysis of serum from vaccinated individuals showed that the two antibody titer measurements were strongly correlated and generally plateaued after day 14 after vaccination.

sources.quote: Antibody titers were measured by both hemagglutination inhibition (HAI) and neutralization assays. The titer results from these assays were strongly correlated, and the titers generally plateaued after day 14.
Because the results for the two antibody titer data sets (HAI and neutralization) were strongly correlated, we combined the information from the two assays for downstream TRI calculations.

groups.assay_method: Hemagglutination Inhibition and Neutralizing Antibody Titer Assay

claim_4.claim: Hemagglutination Inhibition analysis of serum from 92 vaccinated individuals showed that rise in HAI titer had a significant positive relationship with the Titer Response Index compared to lower TRI values (r2 = 0.4585).

sources.quote: The TRI and rise in HAI titer for the 92 individuals show a significant positive relationship (r2 = 0.4585).

claim_5.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of peripheral blood cells / whole blood RNA samples from vaccinated subjects showed that a 494-gene expression signature, including STAT1, CD74, and E2F2, significantly correlated with the magnitude of the antibody response, with STAT1 increasing after vaccination most prominently on day 1 and in high responders and E2F2 being downregulated most prominently on day 3 with greater downregulation in high responders compared to low responders.

sources.quote: We found that the abundance level of 494 transcripts significantly correlated with the TRI (Dataset 8).
Integrative analyses revealed a 494-gene expression signature—including STAT1, CD74, and E2F2—which strongly correlates with the magnitude of the antibody response.

STAT1 expression increases after vaccination, most prominently on day 1 and in the high-responder group. E2F2 expression is downregulated after vaccination, most prominently on day 3 and with greater downregulation in the high-responder group.

groups.tissue_type: peripheral blood cells / whole blood RNA samples

claim_6.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of peripheral blood cells / whole blood RNA samples from high responders compared to low responders showed early upregulation of interferon response and antigen presentation pathways in the high-responder group.

sources.quote: Content analysis of the genes that were upregulated in the high-responder group showed enrichment of GO categories involved in cellular immune responses, most notably the interferon response and antigen presentation pathways (Figure 3A and Datasets 9, 10).
Genes within the interferon response pathway were highly upregulated in the high-responder group (Figure 3B).
High vaccine responder status correlates with increased early expression of interferon signaling and antigen processing and presentation genes.
